Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y=3{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})-3{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+2x+1,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\pi ,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}

feedback.worked_solution:
Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =4x,$ we get

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡8x={cos}^{2}⁡4x-{sin}^{2}⁡4x.
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4-{cos}^{2}⁡4x+{sin}^{2}⁡4x)\text{d}x & =\int (4-[{cos}^{2}⁡4x-{sin}^{2}⁡4x])\text{d}x \\  & =\int (4-\operatorname{cos}⁡8x)\text{d}x \\  & =4x-\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡8x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
